overall: The AG found a de minimis violation for adding a reasonably anticipated topic (minutes approval) to the October 6 notice six minutes late, and no violation on the other allegations; it ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Notice for the October 6 meeting allegedly omitted the date and time it was posted.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the date and time was conspicuously recorded along with the notice, as required by the Open Meeting Law Regulations, and reasonably conveyed that the notice was posted at the listed time.

allegations.summary: The amended notice allegedly did not show both the original posting date and time and the amended posting date and time.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law in this regard.

allegations.summary: The Board allegedly amended the October 6 notice less than 48 hours before the meeting to add a topic that was reasonably anticipated earlier (approval of minutes).
allegations.key_passage: we are constrained to find that the Board committed a de minimis violation of the Open Meeting Law when it added approval of those meeting minutes to the notice for the October 6 meeting six minutes short of 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: The Chair allegedly did not announce that the meeting was being recorded, and the complainant said the word 'recorded' had to be used.
allegations.key_passage: This statement clearly informed attendees that the meeting was being recorded; any assertion to the contrary is not made in good faith.

allegations.summary: The Board allegedly labeled the October 6 meeting an emergency although the subject matter did not meet the statutory definition of an emergency.
allegations.key_passage: because the Board posted notice for its October 6 meeting more than 48 hours in advance of the meeting and was not relying on the Open Meeting Law’s “emergency” exception to the 48-hour notice posting requirement.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
